stem: A Massachusetts collaborative practice agreement names three duties of the authorized pharmacist that may be delegated and two that may not. It says nothing further on the subject. The pharmacist proposes to delegate one of the named duties to trained staff for the next six weeks. What does the agreement still lack?

choices.text: Nothing further, once the delegable and non-delegable duties have been named.
Board approval of this particular delegation before it may take effect.
The when and how of delegation, together with its duration and its scope.
A separate written consent from the patient to the proposed delegation.
The supervising physician's countersignature on the delegation itself.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 16.04(3) imposes a second requirement beyond naming the two categories of duty: the agreement shall specify WHEN AND HOW an authorized pharmacist may delegate duties under the agreement, and the DURATION AND SCOPE of the delegation. Naming the duties is only half of what the paragraph requires.

choice_analysis.A: The paragraph contains a further sentence imposing additional required terms.
choice_analysis.B: No Board approval of an individual delegation is required.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: the when, how, duration and scope must all appear in the agreement.
choice_analysis.D: Patient consent to a delegation is not the requirement in issue.
choice_analysis.E: A countersignature on the delegation is not required by the paragraph.

related_facts: The same paragraph preserves the ordinary intern and technician scope rules
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates stop at the first sentence of the paragraph and treat the naming of duties as the whole obligation.

reasoning_steps: Read past the first sentence of 247 CMR 16.04(3)
Identify the four further particulars the agreement must state
Measure the agreement against all of them
